subject: Multi-region Dedicated — replication costs, routing, and throughput guarantees

Subject: Dedicated — Multi-region sizing & replication cost questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region deployment (US East + EU West) and have a few questions before we build a business case for Procurement:

- We want separate GPU pools per region with active-active routing for reads and active-passive for writes. How do you price replicated capacity vs. primary?
- What are the throughput guarantees per-reserved pool (per-GPU p99 latency, maximum concurrent requests)?
- If we enable cross-region replication (keep K/V caches in sync), is that billed as double capacity or is there a replication license/fee?
- Can you describe failover routing — is it automatic or needs a DNS/manual cutover? Any cost for cross-region routing tiers?

I've attached our initial requirements spreadsheet (CW-Dedicated-Requirements.xlsx). Procurement will want a clear committed-commit vs. burst pricing and an example ARR calc.

Would love a short note on options and an indication of any introductory or multi-region discounts you can extend for a 12–24 month committed contract.

Best,
Emily
Product Ops, CloudWave AI

Subject: Re: Dedicated — Multi-region sizing & replication cost questions

Emily — thanks for the clear doc and questions. Quick summary of options we typically propose for customers with a similar footprint:

1) Separate regional pools (recommended): each region has its own reserved GPU pool sized to expected steady-state throughput. Pricing = base committed units per region + a small cross-region redundancy fee if you enable replication.
2) Geo-replicated pools (hot-hot): full replication across both regions for stateful KV cache (higher cost ~ ~1.7x of single-region commitment depending on cache sync frequency). This gives the shortest failover time and consistent cache hit rates.
3) Active-passive DR standby: primary region carries production traffic; secondary region is reserved at low commit (warm standby) and spun up to full capacity on failover (billing for ramp discussed in license). Lower ARR, but longer RTO.

Throughput guarantees: we provide per-pool p99 latency SLOs and per-GPU throughput baselines. For dedicated pools we guarantee an aggregate throughput target (tokens/s) for the reserved capacity; detailed numbers depend on model family and sequence length — I'll ask Pricing/Engineering to attach the grid.

Routing & failover: we support automated cross-region failover with health-based routing (no manual DNS required) when you enable the multi-region routing add-on. There is a nominal routing tier fee and egress costs for cross-region KV syncs.

I'll loop in Kimberly for formal pricing and an example commit table, and Rishi for the technical routing/DR detail.

-Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emily / team — attaching the price grid (Redwood-Dedicated-Price-Grid-v2.pdf) and a simple ARR calc. High level pricing approach:

- Committed units are quoted per-region as GPU-pool equivalent units (GPE).
- Replication: cold-warm standby = ~30% of committed cost in secondary region; hot-hot = ~70–90% depending on KV sync frequency. We treat KV replication network egress separately and cap it in the contract at a tiered rate.
- Discounting bands: 10% for 12-month commit >= X GPE, 18% for 24-month commit >= Y GPE; additional enterprise rebate for multi-region commit above threshold. We'll propose a blended multi-region discount for CloudWave.
- Burst pricing: metered token-level overages at a fixed per-token rate (we can pre-buy burst credits at a discounted unit price).

I'll include a sample table in the attached PDF that maps committed GPE -> expected p99 and max concurrent model streams for the common model families.

Next steps: if you can confirm target steady-state throughput per region (tokens/s or req/s) we can give a formal quote and an ARR with discount tiers.

Thanks,

Emily — a few technical clarifications to help sizing and the pricing bands:

- KV replication modes: asynchronous (near real-time) vs synchronous (strong consistency). Synchronous replication increases latency and network egress; cost model for synchronous is modeled as additional GPE-equivalent capacity. For most customers, asynchronous with eventual convergence is sufficient and more cost-efficient.
- Routing: our health-based routing uses local pools for lowest latency and optionally routes overflow to the other region. Overflow routing is metered (small per-request uplift) but helps avoid over-committing capacity across regions.
- Warm standby model: keep 25–35% of the peak GPE reserved in the secondary region and enable fast scale-up policy (we've successfully met sub-10min scale to full with autoscaling + pre-warmed caches). The billing during scale-up can be structured to prorate only the incremental hours at committed rates — negotiable in the SOW.

For your spreadsheet, if you share expected p95/p99 latency targets and typical sequence lengths, I can map to concrete GPE numbers and an expected cache hit improvement with replication.

- Rishi

Emily / Amit / procurement team — attaching the single-page summary and the draft SOW excerpt for the multi-region commit. Highlights:

- Proposed commercial: 24-month blended commit across US+EU with a 16% multi-region discount (applies once you hit the two-region GPE threshold).
- Replication model: async KV replication billed as 0.7x GPE for hot-hot; warm-standby priced at 0.3x GPE + capped egress tiers.
- Routing add-on: health-based routing included; overflow metering at $0.002 per routed request beyond committed per-hour allowance.
- SLA: cross-region failover RTO target 5 minutes for health-triggered failover; downtime credits are pro-rated and capped per month in the SOW.
